notes.meaning: God chose Jerusalem as the special place for His temple and capital city. The hills of the city are called holy because the Lord set His presence there among His people. He laid its foundation to be a lasting home for true worship.

The Lord loved Jerusalem and Mount Zion more than any other town or home in Israel. He cared for all His people, but Zion was special because His temple stood there. It was the chosen center where His people gathered together for public praise and prayer.

Wonderful promises and praises have been spoken about Jerusalem, the city of God. The writer pauses with a musical rest to let listeners reflect on its glory. Greater wonders are coming, because God planned to bless people from all nations through this city.

God Himself speaks and lists nations that were once fierce enemies of Israel, like Egypt (called Rahab) and Babylon. He announces that people from these distant lands will truly come to know Him. Instead of being treated as outsiders, they will be welcomed as if they were born right in God's city.

People will say that all kinds of men and women from many nations were born in Zion. This means they are given a fresh start as adopted children in God's family through a spiritual new birth. The Most High God will keep His people safe and make His church firm forever.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early church teachers and later Catholic tradition read the man born in Zion as a prophecy of Jesus Christ, the God-man, who established the Church.

notes.meaning: The Lord keeps an official record of all the people of the earth, like a city census. As He counts His people, He writes beside each believer that they belong to Zion. He counts everyone who trusts Him as a full citizen of His kingdom.

God's people celebrate this great gathering of nations with joyous music, singing, and dancing. They gladly proclaim that every fresh spring of life, peace, and happiness comes from the Lord alone. True joy is found in belonging to God and worshipping Him together.
